Vers la mi-juillet, les présidents lituanien et letton, Gitanas Nauseda et Edgars Rinkevics, ont [USN:L8N43H0SI TEXT:"accusé"] la Russie de projets de sabotage contre des pays de l'Otan, accusations qualifiées par Moscou de "fables alarmistes". Au début de même mois, la Pologne avait dit que les services de renseignement occidentaux s'inquiétaient du risque d'attaques russes contre son territoire et les États baltes. Moscou dément régulièrement ce type d'accusations qui s'inscrivent selon elles dans le cadre d'une campagne de propagande antirusse. Il y a quelques jours, l'Estonie a dit être parvenue à la conclusion qu'un [USN:L8N45L0XL TEXT:"incendie"] ayant eu lieu en août dans les locaux de la société de défense Milrem Robotics, fournisseur de drones terrestres pour l'Ukraine, était un acte criminel commandité par les services de sécurité russes. NÉCESSITÉ DE TROUVER UN ALLIÉ POUR GOUVERNER Réagissant aux résultats des sondages à la sortie des urnes, Andris Kulbergs a déclaré qu’il espérait rester Premier ministre, ajoutant qu'il ne souhaitait pas gouverner avec "Lettonie d'abord". Si les sondages à la sortie des urnes sont confirmés par les résultats officiels, le Premier ministre aura besoin d'alliés pour être en mesure de former un gouvernement. "C'est remarquablement bon. Je ne m'attendais pas à un tel résultat", s'est félicité Andeis Kulbergs au siège de son parti à Riga. Le parti des Progressistes arrive en troisième position dans le classement des sondages à la sortie des urnes, avec également 11,3%, suivi du parti ouvertement pro-russe "Sovereign Power", avec 10,8%. Outre les questions de sécurité, celle du coût de la vie a également dominé la campagne électorale en Lettonie, État membre de l'Otan et de l'Union européenne qui partage une frontière avec la Russie et abrite une importante minorité russophone. Andris Kulbergs, homme d’affaires et pilote de rallye amateur de 47 ans, est arrivé au pouvoir en mai après l'effondrement de la [USN:L6N41R0M0 TEXT:"coalition précédente"], en raison de la façon dont cette dernière avait géré des incidents au cours desquels des drones militaires avaient pénétré dans l'espace aérien letton sans être détectés. Tout au long de sa campagne, il a promis de renforcer les capacités anti-drones de la Lettonie et de maintenir les dépenses de défense à 5% du produit intérieur brut, l'un des niveaux les plus élevés de l'OTAN. La Lettonie, qui compte 1,9 million d'habitants, longe la mer Baltique, avec au nord et au sud l'Estonie et la Lituanie, alliées de l'UE et de l'Otan, et à l'est la Russie et la Biélorussie.

item.title: Fernandes rejects talk of Portugal rift after Ronaldo's abrupt departure
item.description: Bruno Fernandes said on Saturday he had spoken to Cristiano Ronaldo and dismissed suggestions of a rift within Portugal's squad after the captain's abrupt departure from the national team's training camp cast doubt over his international future.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bruno Fernandes said on Saturday he had spoken to Cristiano Ronaldo and dismissed suggestions of a rift within Portugal's squad after the captain's [USN:L6N45M17Z TEXT:"abrupt departure"] from the national team's training camp cast doubt over his international future. Portugal's record goalscorer Ronaldo, 41, left the camp in Copenhagen on Wednesday shortly after coach Jorge Jesus acknowledged tensions between the pair. The Al-Nassr forward departed a day before Portugal's Nations League group-stage clash with Denmark, a match Jesus' side went on to win 4-2. Ronaldo said on Instagram that he made the decision after Jesus' news conference and a conversation with Portuguese Football Federation President Pedro Proenca, adding that he would reveal his reasons "in due course". "I had a chat with him and what I said to him is what I'll repeat here: the most important thing is that, whatever happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football and of the country," Fernandes told a news conference ahead of Sunday's Nations League match against Norway in Porto. "For what he has achieved not only in Portugal, but all over the world. He has a place reserved not only amongst the all-time greats, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people. "The most important thing is that we stop stirring up trouble; there are no divisions within the national team. It is one team and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside." Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Portugal manager Jorge Jesus and Portuguese Football Federation President Pedro Proenca made an [USN:L6N45N0IW TEXT:"unsuccessful dash"] to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade Ronaldo not to leave the squad. "The most important thing is that this ends well, for both sides," the 32-year-old Manchester United captain added. "We're completely out of the picture; we're aware of what you're saying and what we're seeing. We've spent a lot of time in the players' room playing cards; we're on the sidelines of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country doesn't become divided, doesn't take sides, and respects all parties..." Jesus, meanwhile, sought to shift the focus back to Norway. Portugal top Group A4 on nine points from three matches, with Norway third on three. "The focus has to be on the national team, the match against Norway, and what we need to do well, in tune with our people," he said. "But that doesn't mean I'm ignoring Cris. He's a symbol of the Portuguese national team; he's a symbol of Portugal - let that be quite clear. "After the match, there'll be time to talk about that."

item.title: OpenAI safety employee quits, says 'time for trial and error is over'
item.description: A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A former OpenAI safety employee who recently resigned criticized the company's approach to AI safety, arguing that a fast-paced culture focused on rapid development increases the risk of failures. Writing in "I Quit OpenAI Because Its Culture Is Broken," published by the Atlantic on Saturday, David Robinson said AI companies, including OpenAI, were not being "nearly careful enough" and should place greater emphasis on safety expertise and research before developing more capable systems. "The time for trial and error is over," Robinson wrote, arguing that advanced AI systems require safeguards more akin to those used in industries such as nuclear power and aviation. Robinson said OpenAI relies heavily on what it calls "iterative deployment," releasing systems and strengthening safeguards when problems emerge. The comments add to a [USN:L6N45L0PN TEXT:"debate within the AI industry"] over whether companies are moving too quickly to develop increasingly powerful systems. [USN:L4N45L05X TEXT:"OpenAI"] and rival [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:"Anthropic"] have faced scrutiny after incidents in which safety controls failed, or experimental systems behaved unexpectedly. Robinson, who said he spent 3-1/2 years at OpenAI, helped draft the company's preparedness framework and oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier-model launches, wrote: "As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed." "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down," an OpenAI spokesperson said in a statement. Robinson also warned that AI capabilities were advancing faster than researchers' understanding of alignment, a field focused on ensuring AI systems act in accordance with human goals and values.

item.title: Donald Trump says he will attend Georgia-Alabama game
item.description: President Donald J. Trump said he plans to return to Bryant-Denny Stadium next Saturday to attend Alabama's game against Georgia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald J. Trump said he plans to return to Bryant-Denny Stadium next Saturday to attend Alabama's game against Georgia. Trump revealed his plan to visit Tuscaloosa while speaking at the Mitchell Center on the campus of South Alabama in Mobile. "We love Alabama," Trump said. "In fact, we love it so much I'll be here again next Saturday to watch a football game between Georgia and Alabama. "They say it's gonna be a good game. I would think so. Let's see, one is rated No. 2 (Georgia), and one is rated No. 7 (Alabama), but that doesn't matter too much at this stage." Trump is no stranger to this rivalry, as he attended the Crimson Tide's 41-34 win over the Bulldogs in a suite at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Sept. 28, 2024. Trump's announcement comes one week after he attended the Texas-Tennessee game in Knoxville, Tenn. --Field Level Media

item.title: Braves name Dylan Dodd to open NLDS Game 1 vs. Dodgers
item.description: The Atlanta Braves have chosen left-handed reliever Dylan Dodd to open Game 1 of their National League Division Series on the road against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves have chosen left-handed reliever Dylan Dodd to open Game 1 of their National League Division Series on the road against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Saturday. Dodd made no starts in 48 appearances during the regular season, but the Dodgers' batting order features left-handed-hitting sluggers Shohei Ohtani (batting second), Freddie Freeman (fourth), Kyle Tucker (sixth) and Max Muncy (eighth). Switch hitter Tommy Edman is batting ninth. Dodd held left-handed hitters to a .171 average in 2026. He also was effective against right-handed batters, holding them to a .180 average. Overall, Dodd, 28, compiled a 4-1 record and 2.54 ERA in 49 2/3 innings. He struck out 53, walked 14 and allowed seven home runs. The Braves used a similar pitching approach on Thursday in a winner-take-all Game 3 against the Philadelphia Phillies in the wild-card round. They opened with left-handed reliever Ray Kerr, who delivered 3 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and one walk and struck out two. The Braves went on to win the game 6-2 and the series two games to one. It is not known whether Dodd will go that long. His longest outing this season is three innings, which he reached on April 12 and May 23. The Dodgers are going with a conventional starter, ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, against a Braves lineup that features lefty batters Drake Baldwin, Matt Olson and Michael Harris II and switch hitter Ozzie Albies. --Field Level Media

item.title: Barstool's Dave Portnoy blames Ohio State, Ryan Day for 'Big Noon Kickoff' exit
item.description: Barstool Sports and Dave Portnoy will no longer appear on Fox Sports' "Big Noon Kickoff," according to The Athletic.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Barstool Sports and Dave Portnoy will no longer appear on Fox Sports' "Big Noon Kickoff," according to The Athletic. Per the report, Portnoy blamed Ohio State and coach Ryan Day for the decision. "Ohio State has relentlessly complained to Fox," Portnoy said. He added that Ohio State threatened to withhold access to Fox Sports personnel if Portnoy remained on the show. "The juice wasn't worth the squeeze," he added. "(Fox Sports CEO Eric Shanks) and I have a good relationship." Moving forward, the program will feature only the main desk consisting of Urban Meyer, Matt Leinart, Brady Quinn, Mark Ingram II and host Rob Stone. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ancelotti diz estar satisfeito após primeiros amistosos da nova seleção após Copa
item.description: O técnico da seleção brasileira, Carlo Ancelotti, disse estar satisfeito com o desempenho de seus jogadores na primeira turnê desde a eliminação nas oitavas de final da Copa do Mundo, em julho, que terminou com uma vitória por 4 a 0 sobre a Índia no sábado, após duas partidas contra a Austrália.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: O técnico da seleção brasileira, Carlo Ancelotti, disse estar satisfeito com o desempenho de seus jogadores na primeira turnê desde a eliminação nas oitavas de final da Copa do Mundo, em julho, que terminou com uma vitória por 4 a 0 sobre a Índia no sábado, após duas partidas contra a Austrália. Ancelotti fez várias alterações no elenco durante os três amistosos, e todos os jogadores da lista de 26 convocados tiveram tempo de jogo. Apenas Vinícius Júnior e Danilo foram titulares nas três partidas, enquanto oito jogadores fizeram sua estreia pela seleção. Quase dois terços da seleção brasileira que disputou a Copa do Mundo ficaram de fora da turnê, já que Ancelotti iniciou sua jornada para formar a próxima geração da seleção nacional. "Saímos desse período com uma sensação positiva, pois os jogadores tiveram um bom desempenho, embora alguns pudessem ter se saído melhor. Cada jogador tem sua própria personalidade", disse Ancelotti aos repórteres após o término da turnê, que terminou com duas vitórias e um empate. "No fim das contas, estamos satisfeitos. Não importa o nível das partidas; o que importa para nós é nos prepararmos bem para elas e tentarmos dar o nosso melhor, levando em conta todas as circunstâncias... Estou conhecendo esses jogadores muito melhor." Vanderson e Samuel Lino marcaram seus primeiros gols pela seleção, com este último fazendo dois gols contra a Índia, que ocupa a 138ª posição no ranking. "Foi um período muito interessante. Tenho uma ideia muito mais clara para a próxima convocação", disse Ancelotti, referindo-se aos próximos amistosos contra o Japão e Cingapura em novembro. "Obviamente, não faremos muitas mudanças, mas precisamos desenvolver outros jogadores jovens que não estavam na convocação desta vez, mas estarão na próxima", acrescentou ele.

item.title: Lula encerra campanha em São Paulo e diz que disputa é entre "democracia e barbárie"
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) encerrou neste sábado o primeiro turno de sua campanha à reeleição, em São Paulo, com uma caminhada que lotou a rua Augusta, na região central da capital, e defendeu que as eleições de domingo são uma disputa entre “a democracia e a barbárie.”
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) encerrou neste sábado o primeiro turno de sua campanha à reeleição, em São Paulo, com uma caminhada que lotou a rua Augusta, na região central da capital, e defendeu que as eleições de domingo são uma disputa entre “a democracia e a barbárie.” “De um lado está a democracia... e do outro lado está a barbárie e a corrupção”, disse o presidente em uma das suas falas ao longo da caminhada, apesar de, no último dia antes da votação, discursos estarem proibidos. A campanha petista comemorou uma mobilização recorde, maior do que o encerramento da campanha de 2022. Segundo os organizadores, Lula teria conseguido reunir 150 mil apoiadores que lotaram os dois quilômetros da rua Augusta entre a avenida Paulista e a praça Roosevelt. “Tinha muita, muita gente mesmo. É difícil não imaginar que a gente não vai ganhar no primeiro turno... Mas, se não ganhar, o segundo está aí e tem tudo para a gente conseguir ser feliz de novo”, disse Rômulo Lopes, um dos apoiadores do presidente presentes à caminhada. Internamente, a coordenação da campanha de Lula aumentou o otimismo nos últimos dias. Além das pesquisas terem mostrado algum avanço do presidente, o tracking interno, que mede as intenções de voto diariamente, também vem mostrando Lula abrindo alguns pontos em relação ao seu principal oponente, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a ponto de a campanha passar a acreditar que existe alguma chance de uma vitória no primeiro turno. Pesquisa [USN:S0N45F00E TEXT:"CNT/MDA"], divulgada na manhã deste sábado, mostrou Lula com 47,8% dos votos válidos no primeiro turno, contra 42,1% de Flávio. Para vencer já em primeiro turno é necessário que um candidato supere a marca de 50% dos votos válidos, quando são descartados os brancos e nulos. “Amanhã nós vamos ganhar a eleição no primeiro turno e vamos para a (Avenida) Paulista, porque a Paulista é do povo”, disse Lula. A prefeitura de São Paulo, governada pelo prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB), aliado de Flávio, não autorizou o uso da avenida no domingo, depois das eleições. “Ao contrário dos outros países da América Latina, onde a gente viu uma onda de direita no final, aqui no Brasil nós estamos vendo uma onda a nosso favor”, disse o presidente do PT, Edinho Silva. A campanha reconhece, no entanto, que há uma migração de votos de outros candidatos de direita para Flávio Bolsonaro na reta final da campanha, o que é um risco, além da abstenção, que costuma ser maior na população de baixa renda, um grupo que tradicionalmente vota mais em Lula. O presidente vota neste domingo de manhã em uma escola em São Bernardo do Campo, onde sempre manteve seu título, e assiste a apuração em casa. No final da tarde, encontra sua equipe em um hotel na zona central de São Paulo, onde dará uma declaração quando sair o resultado.

item.title: Canadiens, Penguins get together after promising openers
item.description: Two teams that began the season with impressive road victories face off on Saturday when the Montreal Canadiens visit the Pittsburgh Penguins.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams that began the season with impressive road victories face off on Saturday when the Montreal Canadiens visit the Pittsburgh Penguins. Pittsburgh opened its season with a 7-0 win at Philadelphia while Montreal edged the Toronto Maple Leafs, 3-2. The Penguins scored multiple goals in each period against the Flyers and finished with a 38-19 edge in shots on goal. According to OptaSTATS, it was the largest road shutout in a season opener in NHL history. Center Filip Hallander, who missed the majority of last season dealing with a blood clot in his leg, led the way with a goal, two assists and a plus-4 rating while Nicholas Robertson scored twice for Pittsburgh. The victory provided some sweet revenge for the Penguins against the team that knocked them out in six games in the first round of the Stanley Cup playoffs. "I think it meant a lot for us," said goaltender Arturs Silovs, who finished with 19 saves. "We had a bitter taste after the playoffs, and the season opener against the team that knocked us out, everyone knew this was a great opportunity for payback, and we were ready for that." Sidney Crosby, beginning his 22nd season and an NHL record 20th season as captain, had an assist for the Penguins. "I thought we had the right mentality coming into the game," Crosby said. "It's the first game, I don't think anybody expects it to be perfect, but I thought we just had a good work ethic and led with that, and then things just kind of took care of themselves." The Penguins did it without center Ben Kindel (lower-body) and left wing Andrei Kuzmenko, who both practiced Friday and are expected to return to the lineup Saturday. Kindel scored 17 goals and had 35 points as a rookie. To open a spot for Kindel, the Penguins placed center David Gustafsson on waivers. Kuzmenko, a free agent signing who had 13 goals and 25 points with the Los Angeles Kings last season, spent the last 10 days in Russia to mourn the loss of his father, Alexander, who was killed by a brown bear on a fishing trip in southern Siberia. For Montreal, Josh Anderson and Alexandre Carrier each had a goal and an assist and Zachary Bolduc also scored a goal in the Habs' opening win against the rival Maple Leafs. Jakub Dobes finished with 26 saves. "To get a win in the first game, I'm really happy," Canadiens head coach Martin St. Louis said. "Do we have things to address and correct? I'm sure we do, and it's nice to be able to do that after a win. The tone of positivity can stay around and (we can) still do some teaching." Montreal, which heads home after Saturday for a four-game homestand that opens Tuesday against defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina, spent the past three days practicing and taking part in team bonding in Cranberry Township, where the Penguins have their facility. "I think ... it's an opportunity, when you get a break in this kind of schedule, especially early on, (it's important to take it), considering we didn't get a chance to do it during training camp," St. Louis said. "I know we have a close group, but it's about having opportunities to get even closer." --Field Level Media

item.title: West Indies deny India clean sweep as Hope scores unbeaten 162
item.description: Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten 162 off 143 balls as West Indies prevented India from completing a series sweep with a five-wicket victory in the third and final one-day international in New Chandigarh on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shai Hope anchored the chase with an unbeaten 162 off 143 balls as West Indies prevented India from completing a series sweep with a five-wicket victory in the third and final one-day international in New Chandigarh on Saturday. After the early loss of John Campbell in the fifth over, Hope combined with Amir Jangoo for a crucial 109-run stand to steady the innings, helping West Indies reach 78-1 at the end of the powerplay. Jangoo struck his third ODI half-century before being run out for 67, while Sherfane Rutherford fell soon after for 24. Hope, however, maintained the momentum, adding another vital 56-run partnership to keep the chase on track. Despite the dismissals of Keemo Paul and Matthew Forde, Hope remained in control of the chase. Gudakesh Motie contributed a brisk 19 off 14 balls, as West Indies sealed victory with 10 balls to spare. India were forced to rebuild after slipping to 4-2, but Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad steadied the innings with a 137-run partnership. Sharma anchored the recovery with a fluent 92 off 85 balls before falling eight runs short of a century. After Rohit's dismissal, KL Rahul made the most of his lone batting opportunity of the series, bringing up his ninth ODI hundred. Rahul accelerated sharply at the death, smashing 42 runs off the final 12 balls he faced to convert his century into a career-best ODI score. Gaikwad chipped in with a half-century before being dismissed by Jayden Seales. With Rahul unbeaten on 129, India finished strongly through late cameos from Naman Dhir (30 off 21 balls) and Anshul Kamboj (17 off nine balls). Their contributions helped propel India to 351-7, with Rahul and Gurnoor Brar unbeaten at the crease. The Shubman Gill-led side had already secured the series by winning the opening two ODIs. In the second match, India completed a record chase of 406 with 6.3 overs to spare to seal the series.

item.title: Ancelotti happy as friendly tour provides first building blocks of a new Brazil
item.description: Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti said he was satisfied with how his players fared in the first tour since their last-16 exit from the World Cup in July, which ended with a 4-0 win over India on Saturday after two matches against Australia.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti said he was satisfied with how his players fared in the first tour since their [USN:L6N43709V TEXT:"last-16 exit"] from the World Cup in July, which ended with a [USN:L6N45P040 TEXT:"4-0 win over India"] on Saturday after two matches against Australia. Ancelotti heavily rotated his squad during the three friendlies and every player in his 26-man roster got some game time. Only Vinicius Jr and Danilo started all three matches, while eight players made their international debuts. Nearly two-thirds of Brazil's World Cup squad missed the tour as Ancelotti launched his bid to build up the next generation of the national team. "We’ve come out of this period feeling positive because the players performed well, although some could do better. Every player has their own character," Ancelotti told reporters after the tour ended with two wins and [USN:L6N45H0IP TEXT:"a draw"]. "Ultimately, we’re satisfied. It doesn’t matter what standard the matches are at, what matters to us is preparing well for them and trying to do our best, taking all the circumstances into account... I’m getting to know these players much better." Vanderson and Samuel Lino got their first international goals, with the latter scoring a brace against [USN:L6N45O0MC TEXT:"138th-ranked India."] "It’s been a very interesting period. I have a much clearer idea for the next squad selection," Ancelotti said, referring to upcoming friendlies against Japan and Singapore in November. "Obviously, we won’t be making many changes but we need to develop other young players who weren’t in the squad this time but will be next time," he added.

item.title: Furman soccer player's lower leg amputated after injury in match
item.description: Furman University defender Luke Munson had his lower leg amputated after being injured in a match this summer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Furman University defender Luke Munson had his lower leg amputated after being injured in a match this summer. The 19-year-old sophomore sustained the injury in the Paladins' 4-3 win against Duke on Aug. 27 in Durham, N.C. The school confirmed on Thursday that Munson underwent an additional surgery on Wednesday due to complications. "Luke is an incredible young man who means so much to our program and everyone who knows him," head coach Brandon Tucker said. "Our team and the entire Furman Athletics family are rallying around him and his family during this difficult time. Our focus is on supporting him in every way we can as he continues through the recovery process. We ask that everyone respect his privacy and his family's privacy and keep them in your thoughts during this time." Munson confirmed the extent of the injury and announced he was retiring from the sport in a post on Instagram. "I want to say thank you to everyone that I've ever had the honor of sharing a field with and calling my brother," he said. "Thank you to everyone that's been in my soccer journey for the good and the bad because you made me who I am today. Thank you for every team and staff member that gave me a chance to learn. "After another surgery that resulted in having my lower leg amputated, I will no longer be playing the sport that I love. 13 years of amazing experiences with so many amazing people whether that be teammates or opponents. Finally, to the little kid that had dreams of going pro 13 years ago I'm sorry our dream had to end." Munson was making his third start of the season in the game at Duke. He recorded three assists and started 22 games during his freshman season at Furman in 2025. He helped the team finish 16-2-5, winning Southern Conference regular season and tournament titles and earning its first trip to the NCAA College Cup. Prior to joining Furman, Munson spent time with the academies of MLS clubs FC Dallas and Charlotte FC and played for the MLS NEXT Pro side Crown Legacy. --Field Level Media

item.title: Italy's Intesa raises MPS takeover offer price and warns it could drop bid
item.description: Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo raised its takeover offer for Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) on Saturday, saying it would pay shareholders a further €800 million ($900 million) in cash if they reject MPS's counter plan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) raised its takeover offer for Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) (BMPS.MI) on Saturday, saying it would pay shareholders a further €800 million ($900 million) in cash if they reject MPS's counter plan. MPS CEO Luigi Lovaglio is seeking shareholder approval in a vote on October 29 for his strategy opposing the €34 billion share-and-cash offer Intesa announced in June - the biggest transaction so far among a dozen banking deals in Italy over the past two years. Italian takeover rules require Lovaglio to secure shareholder backing before advancing the counter plan he unveiled in August. Lovaglio's strategy envisages MPS making two separate all-share takeover bids for wealth manager Banca Generali (BGN.MI) and rival lender Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) . If MPS shareholders approve either of MPS' two takeover offers on October 29, that would give Intesa the right to drop its own bid based on the conditions to which the bid is subject, Intesa said. "Intesa Sanpaolo does not intend to exercise the right to waive the conditions ... and will claim for their non-fulfilment," it said. Meanwhile, Intesa said it would pay MPS shareholders €1.25 per share, increasing an earlier €1 euro cash component it is offering for each MPS share tendered - on top of the 1.6 newly issued Intesa shares offered for each MPS share they hold. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: France/Lycées Le préfet de police de Paris appelle à des formes d'actions pacifiques
item.description: Le mouvement dans les lycées, protestant contre des conditions d'enseignement dégradées, doit s'en tenir à des "formes d'actions pacifiques", déclare samedi le préfet de police Patrice Faure dans une lettre ouverte, qui condamne les nombreux actes de violence qui ont émaillé la semaine écoulée.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le mouvement dans les lycées, protestant contre des conditions d'enseignement dégradées, doit s'en tenir à des "formes d'actions pacifiques", déclare samedi le préfet de police Patrice Faure dans une lettre ouverte, qui condamne les nombreux actes de violence qui ont émaillé la semaine écoulée. Le ministre de l'Education nationale Edouard Geffray a tenté de calmer la mobilisation dans les lycées en France en recevant vendredi les représentants de syndicats étudiants, qui ont fait part de leur déception et appelé à [USN:L8N45O1H4 TEXT:"poursuivre leur mouvement"]. Tout en se désolidarisant des violences ayant éclaté en marge des blocages d'établissements, ils ont appelé à des rassemblements mardi 6 octobre et seront rejoints par plusieurs confédérations syndicales dont la CGT. Depuis lundi, environ 5.000 personnes, pour la plupart des adolescents, ont été interpellées dans tout le pays et des dizaines d'autres ont été blessées. Agathe Foucault, porte-parole de la police nationale, a déclaré plus tôt dans la journée sur RTL que plus de 600 policiers avaient également été blessés. Au cours des épisodes de violence, des enseignants et des passants ont été agressés, tandis que les dégâts matériels sont estimés à plusieurs dizaines de millions d'euros. "Quoi qu'ils en disent, ceux qui ont impulsé le mouvement ne le contrôlent plus. Il est ainsi plus que temps de revenir à des formes d'actions pacifiques", déclare Patrick Faure. Le mobilisation lycéenne est partie le 18 septembre d'établissements en [USN:L6N45P01N TEXT:"banlieue parisienne défavorisés"] avant de s'étendre au reste du pays. Plus de 400 lycées - sur un total de quelque 3.700 - sont ainsi restés fermés vendredi. "Nous interviendrons quand il le faudra mais il faut à présent que chacun entende quelles sont ses responsabilités", a déclaré Patrick Faure, en appelant également aux parents. Les élèves qui bloquent les lycées dénoncent notamment des classes surpeuplées, le manque d'enseignants ou encore la vétusté des bâtiments, attribuant ces problèmes à des années de sous-investissement dans le secteur de l'enseignement public.

item.title: England crush Croatia 7-0 as Spain stay perfect with Czech victory
item.description: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice apiece as England demolished Luka Modric's Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, but Spain stayed three points clear at the top of their Nations League group with a 3-1 victory over the Czech Republic.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice apiece as England demolished Luka Modric's Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka on Saturday, but Spain stayed three points clear at the top of their Nations League group with a 3-1 victory over the Czech Republic. Jude Bellingham scored once and provided three assists for England, with Anthony Gordon and substitute Morgan Rogers also on target in a performance captain Kane described as "unbelievable". England are second in League A, Group Three with six points from three matches, behind Spain on nine. Croatia have three points and the Czechs remain pointless. "Unbelievable from start to finish," Kane told ITV. "We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game from start to finish, being completely dominant with the ball and without the ball. That was it right there." Kane took his international tally to 89 goals in 124 appearances, moving within one cap of Peter Shilton's England record. Asked about potentially drawing level with Shilton against the Czech Republic on Tuesday, Kane said: "Would be nice. That is why he (manager Thomas Tuchel) takes me off, to save me for the next one!" England went ahead after little more than seven minutes when Josko Gvardiol lost possession and Bellingham released Kane, who slipped between two defenders and fired home. Bellingham doubled the lead in the 21st minute after Gordon turned Saka's cross back across goal. Gordon added the third in the 39th, meeting Jarell Quansah's cross with a first-time finish. Mateo Kovacic squandered a close-range chance before Bellingham crossed for an unmarked Saka to score a minute before halftime. Elliot Anderson supplied Kane's second goal with a low cross in the 53rd minute, before Josip Stanisic's misplaced pass across his own box gifted Saka another goal in the 68th. Bellingham released Rogers to complete the rout three minutes from time. "They couldn't live with our pace, with our runs," Kane said. SPAIN KEEP WINNING World and European champions Spain maintained their perfect start in Oviedo despite coach Luis de la Fuente making nine changes to the side that beat Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday. Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the sixth minute, curling a stunning left-footed shot into the top corner from the edge of the box. After Spain squandered several opportunities, captain Rodri doubled their advantage by converting a rebound inside the area, his first international goal in more than two years. Jiri Slama gave the visitors hope in the 69th minute, finishing a swift counter-attack with an angled shot just inside David Raya's right post. Their chances of an equaliser faded when Ladislav Krejci received a second booking in the 85th minute for holding back an opponent to stop a counter-attack. Mikel Merino then sealed Spain's victory, finishing first time from inside the box following another quick break. In League B, Scotland won 2-0 at North Macedonia through goals from Kieron Bowie and John McGinn before Scott McKenna was sent off in the 83rd minute. Switzerland came from behind to beat Slovenia 2-1 in Luzern, with an Erik Janza own goal and Dan Ndoye's strike overturning Zan Vipotnik's opener. The Swiss lead Group One on nine points, with Scotland and Slovenia level on four.

item.title: Jefe de policía de París dice movimiento de protesta estudiantil está fuera de control, pide actuar de forma pacífica
item.description: El movimiento de protesta estudiantil que se ha extendido por toda Francia está ahora "fuera de control", dijo el sábado el jefe de la policía de París, que instó a los manifestantes a volver a las acciones pacíficas y advirtió de que las autoridades responderían con firmeza ante la violencia y el vandalismo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El movimiento de protesta estudiantil que se ha extendido por toda Francia está ahora "fuera de control", dijo el sábado el jefe de la policía de París, que instó a los manifestantes a volver a las acciones pacíficas y advirtió de que las autoridades responderían con firmeza ante la violencia y el vandalismo. La policía antidisturbios se enfrentó el viernes a estudiantes de secundaria en toda Francia y los sindicatos convocaron una huelga de profesores, mientras el Gobierno del presidente Emmanuel Macron luchaba por contener unas protestas cada vez más violentas por las condiciones en las aulas y la financiación. Desde el lunes, unas 5.000 personas, en su mayoría adolescentes, han sido detenidas en todo el país y decenas han resultado heridas. Agathe Foucault, portavoz de la policía nacional, dijo el sábado a la emisora RTL que más de 600 agentes de policía también habían resultado heridos. Se han producido agresiones contra profesores y ciudadanos, mientras que los daños materiales se estiman en decenas de millones de euros. El jefe de policía de París, Patrice Faure, en una carta abierta publicada en X antes de las nuevas protestas previstas a partir del próximo martes, dijo que quienes habían iniciado el movimiento ya no lo controlaban y pidió a los estudiantes que abandonaran los cierres de colegios y los disturbios en favor de formas pacíficas de protesta. "Es hora de volver a formas pacíficas de acción", escribió Faure, señalando que los padres también tenían la responsabilidad de alejar a sus hijos de lo que describió como la influencia de los "alborotadores profesionales" y sus simpatizantes. Los sindicatos estudiantiles han convocado una jornada nacional de manifestaciones para el martes. Las autoridades de seguridad temen que una protesta organizada en el centro de París, en particular, pueda dar lugar a nuevos actos de violencia, ante la preocupación de que grupos anarquistas de extrema izquierda puedan apropiarse del movimiento. Los estudiantes que bloquean los colegios han expresado su indignación por el hacinamiento en las aulas, la escasez habitual de profesores y el mal estado de los edificios, y culpan de ello a años de falta de inversión.

item.title: Flávio faz motocarreata no interior de SP e diz que vencerá no 1º turno
item.description: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) realizou uma motocarreata entre as cidades de Santa Bárbara D'Oeste e Americana, no interior de São Paulo, neste sábado, e afirmou estar convicto de que será eleito presidente já no domingo, apesar de pesquisas eleitorais apontarem para um segundo turno entre ele e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) realizou uma motocarreata entre as cidades de Santa Bárbara D'Oeste e Americana, no interior de São Paulo, neste sábado, e afirmou estar convicto de que será eleito presidente já no domingo, apesar de pesquisas eleitorais apontarem para um segundo turno entre ele e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Durante o evento, Flávio posou para fotos segurando um cartaz com a imagem de seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que cumpre prisão domiciliar após ser condenado pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) por tentativa de golpe de Estado. "Eu tenho a convicção também que tem tudo pra que a gente ganhe essa eleição já no 1º turno. Então, 'vambora' sair de casa pra votar", disse o senador ao convocar seus apoiadores para irem às urnas no domingo. Flávio estava acompanhado do governador de São Paulo e candidato à reeleição, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), que, segundo as pesquisas recentes, pode ser reeleito já no domingo. Ainda neste sábado, Flávio fará outra motocarreata em bairros da zona norte do Rio de Janeiro. No domingo, ele votará logo cedo em uma escola no bairro carioca de Vila Isabel e deverá acompanhar a apuração em Brasília.

item.title: Solberg leads in Sardinia but Evans still on course for title
item.description: Toyota's Oliver Solberg seized the lead in the world rally championship finale in Sardinia on Saturday but teammate Elfyn Evans remained on course for his first title.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toyota's Oliver Solberg seized the lead in the world rally championship finale in Sardinia on Saturday but teammate Elfyn Evans remained on course for his first title. Hyundai's overnight leader Thierry Neuville crashed out on stage 11, ending a tight battle with Solberg and sending the Swede well clear at the top of the leaderboard as the three-way title battle looked wide open with four stages still to come on Sunday. Evans started the rally 17 points clear of Finland's Sami Pajari, also in a Toyota, and 21 clear of Solberg. As things stood on Saturday evening, Welshman Evans remained on course for the title with his lead reduced to a provisional six points but plenty of potential pitfalls ahead. Solberg led by 33.6 seconds from teammate and reigning nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier, with Pajari third and Evans fifth. Evans had been fourth going into the day's closing stage but lost the place to Hyundai's Adrien Fourmaux, who won the stage. The Frenchman is 52.1 seconds behind Pajari. "Of course now we have to try and change the strategy a bit. Let's see if it is enough," said Evans, who has finished overall runner-up five times in the last six seasons and would be Britain's third rally world champion if he can prevail on Sunday. "I don't think it will be straightforward tomorrow. Today has been a tough day to try and hang in there with Oliver going so fast at the front. We have a long way to go. We have a tough day tomorrow. It is still wide open.” The Alghero-based Italian round is the 13th and final rally of the season after the Saudi Arabia finale was cancelled due to conflict in the region. Toyota have already won the manufacturers' title for the sixth year in a row.

item.title: L'Ukraine va intensifier ses frappes sur les raffineries russes
item.description: L'Ukraine va intensifier ses attaques contre les raffineries russes en réponse à la nouvelle stratégie de frappes aériennes menée par Moscou visant à forcer la population à quitter Kyiv et d'autres villes, sans pour autant prendre pour cible les civils, a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: L'Ukraine va intensifier ses attaques contre les raffineries russes en réponse à la nouvelle stratégie de frappes aériennes menée par Moscou visant à forcer la population à [USN:L8N45P02B TEXT:"quitter Kyiv"] et d'autres villes, sans pour autant prendre pour cible les civils, a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky. Les services de renseignement ukrainiens ont obtenu des documents montrant que le président russe Vladimir Poutine a défini une "nouvelle doctrine" prévoyant des attaques militaires contre un éventail beaucoup plus large de cibles civiles à l'approche de l'hiver, a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky. "Nous avons vu ces documents et nous savons qu'ils leur permettent d'attaquer les infrastructures (...) la logistique (...) les routes, les écoles, les hôpitaux, afin de faire pression sur la population pour qu'elle quitte la capitale et d'autres villes", a-t-il ajouté. D'après la président ukrainien, ce changement de doctrine s'explique par la volonté de Vladimir Poutine de faire une démonstration de force à un moment où son armée perd du terrain sur le front et subit des pertes de plus en plus importantes. Le Kremlin n'était pas disponible samedi pour commenter ces informations. Mais le ministère des Affaires étrangères russe a déclaré plus tôt dans la journée que la Russie continuerait à mener des frappes sur Kyiv et d'autres villes ukrainiennes, exhortant les ressortissants étrangers et les diplomates à quitter la capitale ukrainienne. Les deux parties nient prendre délibérément pour cible des civils. CONTRE-OFFENSIVE DANS LE DONBASS Selon Volodimir Zelensky, une contre-offensive ukrainienne en cours, baptisée "Vivaldi", a permis de reprendre environ 140 kilomètres carrés dans la région du Donbass, dans l'est de l’Ukraine, dont la Russie veut prendre le contrôle intégral. Ces dernières semaines, l'administration du président américain Donald Trump s'est efforcée de relancer les négociations visant à mettre fin à ce conflit - déclenchée par l'invasion à grande échelle de l'Ukraine par la Russie en février 2022 - le plus sanglant que l'Europe ait connu depuis la Deuxième Guerre mondiale. Fin septembre, Volodimir Zelensky s'est entretenu avec Donald Trump en marge de l'Assemblée générale des Nations unies à New York, où ils ont discuté des moyens de mettre fin à la guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie. Le 13 septembre, Donald Trump a appelé Volodimir Zelensky à cesser de prendre pour cible [USN:L6N455055 TEXT:"les raffineries russes"] produisant du diesel, liant implicitement la flambée des prix de ce carburant aux États-Unis à la guerre en Ukraine plutôt qu'au conflit au Moyen-Orient qu'il a déclenché. D'après le président ukrainien, rien d'indique Vladimir Poutine est intéressé par des pourparlers de paix ou par un cessez-le-feu concernant les infrastructures énergétiques. Depuis quelques mois, la Russie a imposé à plusieurs reprises des restrictions sur les exportations d'essence, de kérosène et de [USN:L6N45M0ND TEXT:"gazole"] afin de freiner la hausse des prix des carburants et de remédier aux pénuries provoquées par les attaques de drones ukrainiens contre des raffineries. Mercredi, la Russie a une nouvelle fois pris pour cible le [USN:L8N45M03S TEXT:"réseau énergétique ukrainien"], visant notamment la capitale Kyiv et sa région, faisant sept morts, dont un enfant. Et vendredi, une attaque aérienne russe a fait un mort à Kyiv et a conduit à la fermeture dans la matinée de [USN:L8N45O07U TEXT:"deux ponts"] sur le Dniepr, fleuve traversant la capitale ukrainienne. "Nous devons riposter par tous les moyens (à notre disposition). Face à leurs attaques contre notre secteur énergétique, nous devons riposter en ciblant leur secteur énergétique. En premier lieu, les raffineries de pétrole : ce sont elles qui leur fournissent les fonds nécessaires à cette guerre", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky, s'exprimant en anglais. "Mais nous ne riposterons pas, bien sûr, à l'instar de ce qu'ils font, en visant des cibles civiles", a-t-il ajouté. PAS DE NORMALISATION AVANT UNE PERSPECTIVE DE PAIX Le président ukrainien a exhorté Washington à ne pas normaliser ses relations avec la Russie avant de s'être assuré d'un retour à la paix, réagissant ainsi à l'invitation adressée par Donald Trump à Vladimir Poutine de participer à un sommet du G20 prévu en décembre à Miami. La décision de Washington [USN:L8N44S23E TEXT:"d'autoriser"] Moscou à prendre part début septembre une réunion des pays du G20 tout en interdisant à des journalistes d'y accéder avait déjà irrité certains ministres des Finances de cette instance. Volodomir Zelensky a déclaré qu'il était prêt à rencontrer Vladimir Poutine pour des pourparlers de paix lors du G20, mais il a souligné qu'il ne fallait pas se contenter d'une "normalisation" des rapports avec la Russie. Les responsables ukrainiens notent que la Russie a stocké des centaines de missiles balistiques en prévision d'une offensive hivernale attendue contre les infrastructures électriques et hydrauliques. L'hiver dernier, qui a été le plus dur de la guerre, les frappes russes ont privé de vastes régions du pays d'électricité et de chauffage pendant plusieurs jours d'affilée. Depuis l'été, Moscou a également commencé à lancer chaque jour des dizaines de drones Shahed à réaction, rapides et relativement bon marché, en direction de l'Ukraine, mettant à rude épreuve les défenses anti-aériennes de l'Ukraine. Volodomir Zelensky a précisé que l'Ukraine a eu massivement recours à ses avions de chasse - des F-16 et des MiG - pour abattre environ 60% des drones russes à réaction, tout en ajoutant que les stocks de munitions de 20 mm équipant ces chasseurs s'épuisent. Kyiv travaille d'arrache-pied à la mise au point d'autres solutions - notamment le renforcement de ses capacités de brouillage, a-t-il précisé. La semaine dernière, Volodmir Zelensky a déclaré que l'Ukraine développait cinq modèles de nouveaux drones intercepteurs capables d'abattre les Shahed à réaction. "Nous devrons passer à l'échelle supérieure. J'espère qu'avec tous ces éléments, nous trouverons une solution", a-t-il dit. L'Ukraine a annoncé cette semaine la première utilisation au combat de son propre missile balistique de fabrication nationale, le FP-7, qui dispose d'une portée d’environ 250 kilomètres. Volodomir Zelensky a dit avoir appelé le fabricant de ce missile, Fire Point, pour exhorter ses dirigeants à achever rapidement un modèle à plus longue portée, le FP-9, qui, selon l'entreprise, pourrait atteindre Moscou. "Je leur ai dit : 'Où est mon FP-9 ?'. Nous avons besoin du FP-9. Et le FP-9 sera (prêt) cet automne, j'en suis sûr", a-t-il dit.

item.title: Trump shares Republican senator's phone number in feud over time switch
item.description: US President Donald Trump shared online the supposed phone number of a Republican US senator on Saturday in an escalating dispute over making daylight saving time permanent.
item.dc:creator: Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump shared online the supposed phone number of a Republican US senator on Saturday in an escalating dispute over making daylight saving time permanent. In a social media post, the president urged people to call a phone number he said belonged to Senator Tom Cotton, an Arkansas Republican who opposes the Trump-backed Sunshine Protection Act. The act would end the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour. Trump says most Americans want more afternoon sunlight, but Cotton has argued the change would plunge early risers into darkness in winter. "Everybody in Arkansas, Tom Cotton, a friend of mine, is holding up a very important Bill," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Cotton did not directly respond to Trump's statement, but posted on X: "No one likes changing the clock, me included, but Congress has enacted permanent Daylight Savings Time multiple times before and repealed it each time once Americans experienced absurdly late sunrises in the winter. "Arkansans don't want their kids going to school in the pitch dark, and I'll always put Arkansas first." When Reuters called the number Trump gave for Cotton, it went directly to a voicemail box that did not identify itself as belonging to the senator. Supporters of permanent daylight saving time say adjusting clocks disrupts sleep and increases road accidents, while critics argue later winter sunrises would leave children traveling to school and commuters heading to work in the dark. GOLFING ARGUMENT Trump on Saturday published three Truth Social posts — one in the morning and two in the afternoon — focused on daylight saving time. In a subsequent five-minute session with journalists at the White House, he spent more than half the time talking about the twice-yearly practice of changing clocks by one hour . Most US states have observed the time switch since the 1960s. Clocks this year are slated to switch back to standard time on November 1. "It discombobulates everybody," Trump said, complaining to reporters that losing afternoon daylight caused lateness for meetings and dinner and made it difficult to play more than 14 holes of golf. He also suggested that more daylight would reduce crime. "You know who wants it? The farmers want it. You know who wants it? Sports want it," Trump told reporters before heading to a [USN:L1N45O0PX TEXT:"campaign rally in Ohio"] . "Professional sports and amateurs that would like to play tennis at night, would like to play golf a little bit without having to run home after 14 holes." Trump, an avid golfer, earlier shared an October 1 letter from PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp, writing: "The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments." POLITICAL CONSIDERATIONS After Cotton published his statement, the president responded with a post that framed the matter in political terms. "Give the Republican Party a Senatorial WIN, for a change! … TAKE THE WIN TOM, JUST TAKE THE WIN! YOU NEED IT, AND SO DOES OUR BELOVED REPUBLICAN PARTY!" Trump wrote. Cotton is running for reelection but his race is not considered competitive, as Trump received more than 64% of the Arkansas vote in the 2024 presidential election. The US House of Representatives passed the bill in July, but Cotton is not alone in the Senate. Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, this week called the bill "[USN:L1N45O0H3 TEXT:"dead as disco"]" and said he did not think that Senate Majority Leader John Thune would bring the measure for a vote. The offices of Cotton and Thune did not respond to requests for comment. Saturday's post targeting Cotton is not the first time Trump has shared a senator's phone number to make a point. During his first presidential campaign in 2015, Trump [USN:KCN0PV26U TEXT:"read"] Senator Lindsey Graham's phone number at a rally and dismissed the South Carolina Republican as an "idiot." They later reconciled, with the [USN:L6N43E02O TEXT:"late Graham"] becoming one of Trump's highest-profile allies in Congress.

item.title: Reports: Bears QB Tyson Bagent to start vs. Jets
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is expected to start Sunday's game against the visiting New York Jets, multiple outlets reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is expected to start Sunday's game against the visiting New York Jets, multiple outlets reported on Saturday. Bagent took the majority of the first-team reps at practice this week. He gets the nod over Case Keenum, who passed for 247 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing) in Monday night's 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles after Bagent spent much of the previous week in concussion protocol. Bagent was injured late in the fourth quarter of Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20. He came on in relief of Caleb Williams, who sustained a Grade 2 hamstring strain in that game. Williams has been ruled out for the Bears (2-1) on Sunday against the Jets (1-2). Bagent earned the No. 2 role in training camp but said earlier this week he was not pushing to unseat Keenum, who was given a game ball Monday night. "There's a couple ways to think about it. Obviously, I would like everything that the football world can offer me. But then there's also the part that I am from Shepherd University, so I have absolutely zero ego in this and nobody is a bigger cheerleader and a fan of Case Keenum than I am," Bagent said. "I think he is the epitome of what I believe a quarterback is and is supposed to be. So it was fun to watch him play." Asked on Friday, Bears head coach Ben Johnson did not reveal his QB1 plans. "We'll find out on Sunday," he said. "I know both of them are well prepared to play and win a game for us." Bagent, 26, last started an NFL game during the 2023 season. He went 2-2 in place of former Bears quarterback Justin Fields. In 13 career games, Bagent has completed 65.8% of his passes for 971 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions. --Field Level Media

item.title: Padres' Walker Buehler begins NLDS on paternity leave
item.description: Major League Baseball announced Saturday that San Diego Padres right-hander Walker Buehler has been placed on the postseason paternity list.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major League Baseball announced Saturday that San Diego Padres right-hander Walker Buehler has been placed on the postseason paternity list. During the two-time All-Star's absence, right-hander Randy Vasquez will be on the active roster for the National League Division Series against the Brewers, which begins Saturday night in Milwaukee. Buehler, 32, is permitted to be away from the Padres for one to three days. Upon his return, he will replace Vazquez on the NLDS roster. "Exciting time for him and his wife to be having a baby this weekend, happens to be during the Division Series, which is exciting," San Diego manager Craig Stammen said prior to Game 1. "Don't have any word on what's going on yet but it could happen at any moment. I'm sure there will be stuff that comes out when it does happen. But excited for the Buehler family." Game 1 of the best-of-five series would have been Buehler's turn in the rotation. He held the Brewers to one run on three hits in six innings in an 11-2 victory in San Diego on Aug. 11. Game 2 is Sunday in Milwaukee. The earliest Buehler can pitch is Game 3 when the series shifts to San Diego on Tuesday night. Left-hander Robbie Ray is the Padres' scheduled starter for Game 1, followed by right-hander Michael King for Game 2. Ray will be opposed by hard-throwing right-hander Jacob Misiorowski (16-5, 1.80 ERA), who leads the majors in ERA and strikeouts (252 in 174 2/3 innings). Buehler's wife, McKenzie, is expected to give birth to their second child on Saturday, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Their daughter, Finley, was born in January 2024. Buehler stayed behind in San Diego when the club traveled to Milwaukee. "I think we didn't want Walker having to pitch on a possible day of the birth of his child and miss that," Stammen said. "I think it made sense that he's able to stay in San Diego and allow that to happen and not having to worry about pitching and that going on at the same time." Buehler was 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA in 32 starts in his first season with the Padres. A two-time World Series champion with the Los Angeles Dodgers, Buehler did not pitch in the NL wild-card sweep against the Chicago Cubs. He is 4-4 with a 3.04 ERA in 19 appearances (18 starts) in the postseason. Vasquez, 27, was 10-6 with a 3.90 ERA in 32 games (23 starts) this season for San Diego. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pirata informático de ShinyHunters, implicado en robo de datos del FBI, detenido en Jordania: fuentes
item.description: Un presunto miembro del grupo de piratas informáticos ShinyHunters, que afirma haber robado datos de todos los empleados del FBI, fue detenido esta semana en Jordania y está cooperando con la agencia de investigación, informaron a Reuters tres personas familiarizadas con el asunto.
item.dc:creator: Jana Winter, Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Un presunto miembro del grupo de piratas informáticos ShinyHunters, que afirma haber robado datos de todos los empleados del FBI, fue detenido esta semana en Jordania y está cooperando con la agencia de investigación, informaron a Reuters tres personas familiarizadas con el asunto. Saif al-Din Khader fue detenido por las autoridades jordanas, según las tres fuentes. Dos de ellas afirmaron que fue puesto bajo custodia el martes. Reuters no pudo determinar de inmediato las circunstancias de la detención de Khader ni el lugar donde se encuentra recluido. Dos fuentes señalaron que está colaborando con el FBI y las fuerzas del orden internacionales para localizar a los demás hackers del grupo. El FBI se negó a hacer comentarios sobre ninguna detención o actividad concreta en el extranjero, pero dijo que la agencia "sigue investigando de forma enérgica el reciente incidente cibernético en el que presuntamente están implicados los ShinyHunters, habiendo colaborado ya con sus socios para detener a varios sospechosos, y no escatimaremos recursos para llevar ante la justicia a cada uno de los responsables". Los intentos de Reuters por contactar con Khader y con miembros de su familia durante la última semana y media han sido infructuosos. La detención de Khader, cuyo supuesto apodo de hacker es Rey, supone un nuevo giro en el caso de ShinyHunters. Los expertos creen que este prolífico grupo de ciberchantaje, que cuenta con un largo historial de ataques contra grandes empresas de todo el mundo, está formado principalmente por jóvenes hackers angloparlantes especializados en el robo de datos y la extorsión. Su robo de lo que, según afirman, son montañas de datos sobre todos y cada uno de los empleados del FBI ha suscitado comparaciones con la intrusión, presuntamente vinculada a China, en la Oficina de Gestión de Personal de Estados Unidos en 2015, que puso en peligro datos confidenciales de millones de estadounidenses que habían sido sometidos a controles de seguridad. INFORMACIÓN SENSIBLE Un análisis de Reuters de una muestra de los datos compartidos por ShinyHunters reveló que estos contenían una gran cantidad de información de identificación personal de los empleados del FBI, datos confidenciales sobre sus funciones laborales e información psiquiátrica y médica. La cooperación de Khader con los investigadores podría ser fundamental para ayudar a contener, o al menos comprender, el daño. Una fuente dijo que estaba guiando a los investigadores a través de sus dispositivos electrónicos y su correspondencia digital para ayudar al FBI a localizar a sus cómplices. "Su cooperación es fundamental para los esfuerzos en curso destinados a detener a estos hackers", dijo la fuente a Reuters. Desde hace días había indicios de que ShinyHunters estaba sufriendo trastornos tras el anuncio de su intrusión en el FBI. A partir del martes, Reuters no pudo ponerse en contacto con ShinyHunters a través de la cuenta en línea que utilizaba anteriormente para comunicarse con los periodistas. Posteriormente, el miércoles, desapareció el sitio web de la dark web del grupo, donde anteriormente había publicado amenazas contra el FBI. El director del FBI, Kash Patel, había insinuado que se producirían más detenciones tras el anuncio de que otro presunto miembro de ShinyHunters, Pepijn van der Stap, había sido detenido en los Países Bajos.

item.title: Sinner se retira del Masters de Shanghái debido a su lesión de rodilla
item.description: El número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, se retiró del Masters de Shanghái de la próxima semana, ya que sigue recuperándose de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido apartado de las pistas desde que ganó el título de Wimbledon en julio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, se retiró del Masters de Shanghái de la próxima semana, ya que sigue recuperándose de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido apartado de las pistas desde que ganó el título de Wimbledon en julio. El italiano, de 25 años, no ha jugado desde su triunfo en el All England Club, por lo que se ha perdido la gira norteamericana sobre pista dura, incluido el Abierto de Estados Unidos, y el torneo ATP 500 que se está disputando actualmente en Pekín. "Por desgracia, este año no podré jugar en el Rolex Shanghái Masters como esperaba", escribió Sinner el sábado en Instagram. "Siempre disfruto jugando ante el público de Shanghái y lamento mucho no poder hacerlo la semana que viene". El torneo Masters 1000 se celebra del 7 al 18 de octubre y cuenta con un potente cuadro encabezado por el cuatro veces campeón Novak Djokovic, junto con Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvédev, Ben Shelton, Félix Auger-Aliassimey el vigente campeón, Valentin Vacherot. Sinner se alzó con el título de Shanghái en 2024, tras derrotar a Djokovic en la final. La ausencia de Sinner podría dar un impulso a las aspiraciones de Zverev de terminar la temporada como número uno del mundo. El alemán, campeón este año de Roland Garros y del Abierto de Estados Unidos, se ha convertido en el rival más cercano del italiano. Zverev puede avanzar a lo más alto de la clasificación por primera vez si gana tanto el Abierto de China en Pekín como el Masters de Shanghái.

item.title: Paris police chief says student protest movement out of control, urges peaceful action
item.description: Patrice Faure said the people who launched the movement no longer controlled it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The student protest movement that has spread across France is now "out of control", the Paris police chief said on Saturday, urging demonstrators to return to peaceful action and warning that authorities would respond firmly to violence and vandalism. [USN:L1N45O03R TEXT:"Riot police"] clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly violent protests over classroom conditions and funding. Since Monday, around 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested nationwide and dozens injured. Agathe Foucault, a spokesperson for the national police, told RTL radio on Saturday that more than 600 police officers had also been injured. Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the tens of millions of euros. Paris police chief Patrice Faure, in an open letter published on X ahead of planned renewed protests from next Tuesday, said those who had launched the movement no longer controlled it and called on students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest. "It is time to return to peaceful forms of action," Faure wrote, saying parents also had a responsibility to steer their children away from what he described as the influence of "professional rioters" and their supporters. Student unions have called for a national day of demonstrations on Tuesday. Security officials fear that an organised protest in central Paris in particular could see further violence amid concerns that far-left anarchist groups could hijack the movement. [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"The students blockading"] high schools have voiced anger over overcrowding in classrooms, regular shortages of teachers and dilapidated buildings, blaming years of underinvestment.

item.title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed execution
item.description: The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's [USN:L1N45O0WH TEXT:"failed attempt to execute"] her by lethal injection. The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers wrote in a Friday court filing. It is the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to halt attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026. Lee said on Saturday that Frank Strada has resigned as Department of Correction commissioner and would leave his position this month. The governor had ordered an independent review of the execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. Strada, in a separate statement, said that although he believes his agency's personnel followed proper protocol, "stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward." An interim commissioner will be announced later, the governor's office said. "Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment,” Lee said in a statement. Pike's lawyers have accused Correction Department officials of ignoring prior warnings from her doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis would make placing intravenous lines especially difficult. Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995, when Pike was 18. Doctors were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her lawyers said on Friday.

item.title: Brasil vence 4-0 a India en partido amistoso, en debut goleador de Samuel Lino con la selección
item.description: Samuel Lino marcó sus dos primeros goles con la selección de Brasil, mientras que el frenético esfuerzo de la India por contener a los cinco veces campeones del mundo se desvaneció tras un comienzo enérgico, lo que permitió a los visitantes llevarse una cómoda victoria por 4-0 en un partido amistoso disputado el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: Samuel Lino marcó sus dos primeros goles con la selección de Brasil, mientras que el frenético esfuerzo de la India por contener a los cinco veces campeones del mundo se desvaneció tras un comienzo enérgico, lo que permitió a los visitantes llevarse una cómoda victoria por 4-0 en un partido amistoso disputado el sábado. El extremo del Chelsea Estevao marcó el primer gol de Brasil y asistió a Pedro antes de que Lino anotara un doblete en la segunda parte, lo que ayudó al equipo de Carlo Ancelotti a concluir su gira por Australia e India con dos victorias y un empate. Ancelotti, que fue probando diferentes combinaciones en la plantilla durante los tres amistosos, realizó ocho cambios respecto a la victoria del martes por 4-2 sobre Australia, manteniendo únicamente a Vinícius Jr., Danilo y Gabriel Bontempo. La estrategia de la India de dejar a Vinícius sin tanta marca por la izquierda y tenderle trampas de fuera de juego tuvo un cierto éxito inicial, ya que combinaron a sus defensas con un centro del campo bajo para contener a Brasil y buscaron al único delantero, Manvir Singh, con pases en profundidad. Pero Estevao abrió el marcador en el minuto 28, recortando desde la derecha para rematar con la izquierda al primer palo, antes de asistir en el segundo gol de Brasil con un pase que rompió la defensa y que Pedro convirtió en gol. Pedro asistió a Samuel Lino para el tercer gol cerca de la hora de juego, antes de que el extremo del Flamengo, de 26 años, regateara a dos defensas para poner el 4-0 justo antes del final del partido, mientras los 51.000 espectadores del Salt Lake Stadium animaban a los visitantes con el mismo entusiasmo que a su propia selección. India, número 138 del mundo, se quedó lamentando las ocasiones falladas, ya que Manvir y Ryan Williams no lograron marcar un gol de consuelo, prolongando además su racha sin victorias a seis partidos.

item.title: Vanderbilt QB Blaze Berlowitz to start vs. No. 2 Georgia
item.description: Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis has been ruled out of Saturday's game at No. 2 Georgia in Athens due to an undisclosed injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis has been ruled out of Saturday's game at No. 2 Georgia in Athens due to an undisclosed injury. Blaze Berlowitz will get the nod in place of Curtis, who flipped his commitment from the Bulldogs to the Commodores in December in a surprise that helped signify Vanderbilt's rise from the Southeastern Conference basement. Berlowitz has completed 14 of 25 pass attempts for 178 yards this season for the Commodores (3-1, 0-1). Curtis, 19, has thrown for 746 yards and four touchdowns with three interceptions, and he has rushed for two scores across his first four career games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Latvia PM's United List ahead in election, exit poll shows
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List looked set to win Saturday's election for parliament, as widely expected, but must build a coalition with other parties to stay in power, an exit poll showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List looked set to win Saturday's election for parliament, [USN:L8N45L1R2 TEXT:"as widely expected"], but must build a coalition with other parties to stay in power, an exit poll showed. Security concerns and cost of living issues have dominated the election agenda in Latvia, a NATO and European Union member state which borders Russia and is home to a significant Russian-speaking minority.

item.title: Colts downgrade WR Keenan Allen to out vs. Commanders
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out Keenan Allen for Sunday's game in London against the Washington Commanders and elevated fellow wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out Keenan Allen for Sunday's game in London against the Washington Commanders and elevated fellow wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad. Allen, 34, was downgraded from questionable as he nurses a groin injury. He has 13 catches for 100 yards and a touchdown this season for the Colts (1-2) after signing a one-year contract on Aug. 18. A six-time Pro Bowl selection, Allen has 1,068 career receptions for 12,151 receiving yards and 71 touchdowns in 174 games with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2013-23, 2025), Chicago Bears (2024) and Colts. Westbrook-Ikhine, 29, also was elevated from the practice squad to play in last Sunday's 19-17 victory over the Houston Texans. He joins Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin and Darius Slayton as receivers available to play versus the Commanders (1-2). --Field Level Media

item.title: Ucrania atacará las refinerías rusas en respuesta a la "nueva doctrina" de Moscú sobre ataques aéreos
item.description: Ucrania redoblará sus ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas en respuesta a una nueva política de ataques aéreos por parte de Moscú, destinada a obligar a la población a abandonar Kiev y otras ciudades, pero no atacará a civiles, dijo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ucrania redoblará sus ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas en respuesta a una nueva política de ataques aéreos por parte de Moscú, destinada a obligar a la población a abandonar Kiev y otras ciudades, pero no atacará a civiles, dijo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski. Los servicios de inteligencia ucranianos han obtenido documentos que demuestran que el líder ruso, Vladimir Putin, había emitido una "nueva doctrina" de ataques militares contra una gama mucho más amplia de objetivos civiles de cara a este invierno boreal, señaló Zelenski. "Hemos visto los documentos y sabemos que les permiten atacar infraestructuras... logística... carreteras, colegios, hospitales, para presionar a la población a que abandone la capital y otras ciudades", afirmó Zelenski. "Ese es el objetivo de la operación". Según Zelenski, lo que impulsó este cambio de política fue el deseo de Putin de aparentar fortaleza en un momento en que su ejército estaba perdiendo terreno en una región clave del frente y sufriendo un mayor número de bajas. El Kremlin no estuvo disponible para hacer declaraciones el sábado. Sin embargo, en un comunicado en el que instaba a los ciudadanos extranjeros a abandonar Kiev, el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores ruso dijo que Moscú seguiría atacando sistemáticamente objetivos en lo que calificó de ataques de represalia por los ataques ucranianos contra Rusia en los últimos meses. Ambas partes niegan haber atacado deliberadamente a civiles. CONTRAOFENSIVA EN DOMBÁS Zelenski dijo que una contraofensiva ucraniana en curso, cuyo nombre en clave es "Vivaldi", había recuperado unos 140 km² de la región oriental ucraniana del Dombás, sobre la que Rusia ha declarado que debe ejercer un control total como condición para cualquier acuerdo de paz. En las últimas semanas, la Administración del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump ha intentado reactivar las negociaciones para poner fin al conflicto, que ya dura cuatro años y es el más sangriento de Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial. El mes pasado, el líder estadounidense instó a Ucrania a abstenerse de atacar las instalaciones petroleras rusas, alegando que ello estaba provocando una subida vertiginosa de los precios mundiales del diésel. Sin embargo, Zelenski, en declaraciones realizadas mientras sonaban las sirenas antiaéreas fuera de los salones dorados de la presidencia, dijo que no había recibido ninguna señal por parte de Rusia de que Putin estuviera interesado en las negociaciones de paz ni en discutir un alto el fuego en relación con las infraestructuras energéticas. Durante la última semana, la capital ucraniana ha sido objeto de ataques persistentes por parte de drones y misiles rusos dirigidos contra activos energéticos y de telecomunicaciones, así como sobre infraestructuras viarias y ferroviarias. Por primera vez, Rusia ha atacado los puentes que cruzan el río Dniéper y conectan el este y el oeste de Kiev. Zelenski afirmó que Ucrania respondería al cambio de táctica de Moscú, pero que no respondería de la misma manera atacando indiscriminadamente infraestructuras civiles. "Tenemos que responder de cualquier forma (que podamos). Ante sus ataques contra nuestro sector energético, tenemos que responder atacando el suyo. En primer lugar, las refinerías de petróleo: lo que les proporciona los fondos para esta guerra", dijo Zelenski en inglés. "Pero, por supuesto, no responderemos, al igual que ellos, atacando objetivos civiles". APOYO DE EUROPA Después de que la Administración Trump invitara a Putin a asistir a la cumbre del G20 en Miami en diciembre y discutiera acuerdos comerciales con los enviados rusos, Zelenski instó a Washington a no normalizar las relaciones con Rusia antes de garantizar el retorno a la paz. Zelenski aseguró que estaría encantado de reunirse con Putin para mantener conversaciones de paz en el G20, pero advirtió a Estados Unidos que no se hiciera ilusiones de que Rusia pondría fin a las hostilidades si conseguía el control del Dombás. "No es justo simplemente normalizarlo", afirmó Zelenski, vestido con su característica camiseta negra y chaqueta de estilo militar. Cualquier reanudación de los lazos económicos y diplomáticos con Occidente debía ser a cambio de la paz, señaló: "Porque la paz es más importante que cualquier tipo de economía". Aunque Estados Unidos ha propuesto reanudar las conversaciones trilaterales en las próximas semanas en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Zelenski señaló que aún no se había fijado una fecha ni un lugar concretos para las conversaciones a nivel técnico. Las autoridades ucranianas advierten de que Rusia ha acumulado cientos de misiles balísticos de cara a una esperada ofensiva invernal frente las infraestructuras eléctricas y de agua. En el invierno boreal pasado, el más duro de la guerra, los ataques rusos dejaron amplias zonas del país sin electricidad ni calefacción durante días. Desde el verano boreal, Moscú también ha comenzado a lanzar cada día sobre Ucrania decenas de drones Shahed propulsados por reactores, rápidos y relativamente baratos, ante los que las defensas aéreas ucranianas han tenido dificultades, ya que su anterior generación de drones interceptores era demasiado lenta para alcanzarlos. Zelenski dijo que Ucrania se había visto obligada a depender en gran medida de sus aviones de combate, F-16 y MiG, para derribar alrededor del 60% de los drones rusos propulsados por reactores, pero que las reservas de munición de 20 mm para los aviones se estaban agotando. Kiev estaba trabajando con urgencia en otras soluciones, entre ellas reforzar sus capacidades de interferencia, dijo. En la segunda quincena de octubre, recibiría el primer envío de misiles de defensa aérea pequeños y económicos capaces de derribar los nuevos Shahed. La semana pasada, Zelenski dijo que Ucrania estaba desarrollando cinco modelos de nuevos drones interceptores capaces de derribar los Shahed a reacción. Tras una reunión con sus jefes de defensa, señaló que las pruebas realizadas con dos de esos modelos habían mostrado una tasa de éxito modesta, de alrededor del 30%. "Tendremos que ampliar la escala", dijo. «Espero que con todo esto, con todos estos elementos, encontremos una solución". AMENAZA BALÍSTICA Ucrania anunció esta semana el primer uso en combate de su propio misil balístico de fabricación nacional: el FP-7, que tiene un alcance de unos 250 kilómetros.
